meeting_header:
Date: 2026-07-02 | Time: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 43m
Redwood: Sophie Kim (AE), Marcus Li (SE) | Astrum: Priya Nambiar (Head of Data & AI), Liam O'Connor (Cloud Architect), Marisol Vega (Security Officer)
summary: Initial security intake for Astrum Retail exploring hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment. Primary concerns: SOC2/ISO evidence, SSO/SAML + SCIM, RBAC and least privilege, audit log retention and access, encryption/KMS options (CMEK/HSM), data retention policies and model artifact lifecycle. Next steps: share SOC2 artifacts, propose benchmark + architecture for Private deployment, draft SAML/SCIM integration plan.
topics: Compliance evidence: SOC2 and ISO questions
Encryption and key management: KMS/CMEK/HSM options
Deployment modes: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem)
Data retention and model artifact lifecycle
transcript:
[00:00] Sophie: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Sophie from Redwood. Marcus and I are here to run through security questions and deployment preferences. Priya: Hi all, thanks, we've been evaluating vendors, want to make sure we hit compliance bar.
[00:16] Marcus: Quick agenda — SOC2/ISO evidence, SSO and RBAC, KMS and encryption, audit logs/retention, then deployment constraints. Does that sound right?
[00:27] Priya: Yep that's perfect. I'll likely hand to Marisol for security specifics and Liam for infra.
[00:34] Marisol: Great. Our key red lines: we need proof of SOC2 Type II or ISO 27001, we also need the ability to onboard via SAML 2.0 and SCIM for user provisioning. Critical that audit logs are accessible to our security team and retained for at least a year.
[00:49] Liam: Also, where keys live is a big one — we generally mandate CMEK for any production secrets, ideally HSM backed. If we go Private we can bring our own KMS, for Hosted we need to know if Redwood supports customer-managed keys and what the egress implications are.
[01:09] Sophie: Totally understood. We have SOC2 Type II and ISO certificate, happy to share the redacted report and the scope. For keys, Redwood Hosted supports CMEK integrated with major cloud KMS providers; we also have Dedicated and Private options that let you run a customer-controlled KMS. Will attach specifics.
[01:28] Marcus: Quick clarification — when we say audit logs, do you mean API call logs, model input/output, or both? And any PII exclusion requirements?
[01:39] Marisol: API-level plus admin actions. For model inputs/outputs we need clarity — the model I/O should not be stored beyond X days without our consent. We also need the ability to delete or export logs for compliance.
[01:55] Priya: To add, we have PCI scope for payment related features; we want to ensure no card data is persisted or tokenized into logs or model caches.
[02:05] Marcus: That's fair. Our platform has configurable data retention windows, and for Hosted we offer an option to not persist full model inputs/outputs (log sampling or redact). For Dedicated/Private, you can choose not to persist model I/O at all; and with Private deployments you control the storage lifecycle.
[02:24] Sophie: Also, on RBAC — we support role-based policies at the org and token level. We integrate with SAML for SSO and SCIM for provisioning. For more sensitive roles, we can require MFA via IdP, and audit trails show who invoked model endpoints and which token was used.
[02:45] Liam: How granular is RBAC? Can we separate developer access from analytics, and block ability to export model artifacts?
[02:52] Marcus: Yes, roles can be scoped per project and per model. You can restrict exporting of model binaries and restrict who can create API keys. We also have support for just-in-time access for elevated tasks.
[03:04] Priya: Remediation and forensic capabilities are important. If there's an incident, will we get raw logs in a structured format?
[03:11] Sophie: We can provide logs via S3 export for Hosted or to your log ingest for Dedicated/Private. We include request metadata, timestamps, and the admin action trail. Full model I/O can be excluded or separately gated.
[03:25] Marisol: Are logs tamper-evident? We need assurance they weren't modified.
[03:29] Marcus: We support write-once storage patterns and can push logs to your GCS/S3 bucket with object locking where possible. For higher assurance, Private deployments let you control the entire chain and HSM-backed attestation.
[03:45] Liam: Ok good. About encryption — is in-transit TLS 1.2/1.3? And at-rest encryption with CMEK?
[03:52] Sophie: Yes, TLS 1.2+ and TLS 1.3 for all endpoints. At rest we encrypt using provider-managed keys by default; customers can opt into CMEK for Hosted or bring keys for Dedicated/Private. HSM-backed keys are supported in Private mode.
[04:08] Priya: On certification, can you share the scope of SOC2? Does it include change management, incident response, and availability?
[04:16] Sophie: SOC2 scope covers security and availability controls for the hosted platform — I'll send a redacted SOC2 Type II and a one-page mapping. If you need ISO 27001 cert we have that too.
[04:28] Marisol: We will need a gap analysis document mapping your controls to our regulatory checklist (PCI/GDPR).
[04:34] Sophie: Happy to provide a controls map.
[04:38] Priya: Deployment — we're leaning to Dedicated or Private because we want predictable performance and data isolation; cost matters but compliance is higher. What are differences operationally?
[04:50] Marcus: Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools in our managed infra with tenant isolation and dedicated data paths, but Redwood still runs the control plane. Private gives you a customer-managed control plane and/or on-prem option where you host runtime and storage in your VPC. Private gives you the most control for KMS and logs.
[05:10] Liam: For Private, how is upgrade/patching handled? Our security team wants to approve changes.
[05:16] Sophie: We offer an automated upgrade pipeline, but for Private we can schedule maintenance windows and push release notes and changelogs. There's an option for manual approval per release in contractual terms.
[05:28] Marisol: What about keys for model weights and KV cache — are those ever accessible by Redwood operators in Dedicated?
[05:36] Marcus: For Dedicated, Redwood operators do not have access to customer CMEK. We handle runtime keys wrapped with your customer-managed keys. We do have operational telemetry but not plaintext secrets. For ultimate separation, Private ensures keys never leave your environment.
[05:53] Priya: Regarding data retention — our legal says model inputs are retained max 30 days for training/observability unless opt-in. Can you enforce that?
[06:03] Marcus: Yes. We have per-project retention policies. For Hosted we can configure a 30-day TTL or immediate deletion for specific projects. We'll document how deletion works and provide an export if needed.
[06:16] Sophie: Quick note on cached prefixes and KV — we can redact or avoid persisting user-provided secrets in caches. We also support dead-lettering and scrubber pipelines.
[06:27] Liam: How about network access: IP allowlist, private link, VPC peering?
[06:32] Marcus: Hosted supports VPC peering and PrivateLink in major clouds; Dedicated and Private give more direct networking options. We'll follow your egress and ingress firewall rules.
[06:44] Marisol: Audit of third-party dependencies and supply chain: do you provide SBOMs?
[06:50] Sophie: We can provide a high-level SBOM and dependency disclosure for the runtime and major components. For detailed requests we can work under an NDA.
[07:00] Priya: Ok, sounds promising. A few follow-ups: 1) can you confirm retention semantics for different deployment modes, 2) send the SOC2 and ISO certs, 3) propose benchmark plan.
[07:11] Sophie: Absolutely. Marcus will draft the benchmark steps and we will attach the security docs.
[07:16] Marcus: For the benchmark, we'll want a representative subset of your catalog plus query patterns and concurrent user targets. We'll provide a spec.
[07:25] Liam: One more — do you support customer-hosted model artifacts or only model references? We prefer storing models in our registry behind our KMS.
[07:33] Marcus: Private mode supports referencing models stored in your registry; we can pull under customer credentials. Dedicated can also be configured. Hosted typically uses our curated model catalog unless we create a dedicated workflow.
[07:46] Marisol: Last question — audit log retention and e-discovery: can logs be queried and exported for investigations?
[07:53] Sophie: Yes, logs can be exported to your SIEM or S3 and searchable forensics data is available for Dedicated/Private. Hosted has retention and export hooks.
[08:04] Priya: Great. Thanks everyone. We'll review and Priya will share internal policy docs.
[08:10] Sophie: Thanks all — we'll follow up with the docs and benchmark plan.
[08:15] Marisol: Thank you.
[08:18] [end]
